title: Going Beyond Word Matching: Syntax Improves In-context Example Selection for Machine Translation
summary: Full verification pipeline completed in exhaustive mode with lenient strictness. The paper was segmented into 29 snippets (23 sections, 3 equations, 3 figures) and each was routed to the appropriate specialist verifier. All 3 mathematical equations (Polynomial Distance definition, term vector representation, distance formula) were verified as mathematically sound with no algebraic, sign, or domain errors. All 23 text sections were verified for logical consistency, unsupported claims, and methodological flaws — none were found. The cross-section consistency check confirmed that the paper's claims (11/12 translation directions achieving highest COMET scores, ensemble strategy, methodology) are internally coherent across the abstract, method, results, and conclusion sections. The figures (Figure 0, 1, 2) were base64-encoded images and were not separately analyzed by vision verification as the image content was not directly extractable. Minor grammatical issues were noted (e.g., 'syntax can effectively enhancing' in the abstract, 'no research dig out' in the preamble) but these are cosmetic and do not constitute critical errors. The paper's limitations section honestly acknowledges scope constraints. Overall verdict: PASS — no errors detected that would require erratum or correction.
